lead: Drilling and milling both spin a multi-point cutter, but the work moves differently. A drill feeds along its own axis to make a hole. A milling cutter feeds sideways across the work on a table, so it makes flat faces, slots and profiles. The direction of table feed against cutter rotation separates up milling from down milling. These processes appear in every workshop: bolt holes in a pump body, keyways in a shaft, flat faces on a gearbox cover. The same speed, feed and time formulas serve manual and CNC machines.
prereq: You need: 5.1 for chip formation and 5.6 for rotation and feed.

sections.h3: Drilling: one rotating tool, many hole operations

blocks.text: Drilling makes a hole with a rotating tool fed along its axis. The common twist drill has a shank, a body with two helical flutes, and a point. The flutes curl chips out and carry cutting fluid in. The point angle is 118° for general steel; the chisel edge at the centre does little cutting and needs a small approach allowance. Helix angle sets the rake face and chip flow. A drill usually makes a slightly rough, slightly oversize hole.

Other hole operations use the same spindle. Reaming removes a small stock with a multi-edge reamer to improve size and finish. Boring enlarges a hole with a single-point tool and can correct its position. Counterboring makes a flat-bottom cylindrical enlargement for a socket-head screw. Countersinking makes a conical enlargement for a flat-head screw. Tapping cuts an internal thread with a tap. Drilling starts the hole; reaming and boring follow it when accuracy matters.
N = 1000v/(πD); feed rate = fN; time = (L + A)/(fN); MRR = (π/4)D² fN
blocks.where: N is spindle speed in rev/min; v is cutting speed in m/min; D is drill diameter in mm; f is feed in mm/rev; L is plate thickness in mm; A is approach in mm; feed rate is in mm/min; time is in min; MRR is material removal rate in mm³/min.

sections.h3: Milling and the two feed directions

blocks.text: Milling uses a rotating multi-tooth cutter while the work is clamped to a table that feeds. In horizontal milling the spindle is horizontal and a slab cutter on an arbor makes a flat surface. In vertical milling the spindle is vertical; a face mill makes large flat faces and an end mill makes slots, pockets and profiles. A slot cutter cuts narrow slots and a form cutter carries the contour it must leave. The table feed per tooth is f<sub>z</sub>; for z teeth at N rev/min the table feed is f<sub>z</sub>zN mm/min.

Up milling (conventional milling) has the table feed opposite to cutter rotation at the cut. The tooth starts at zero chip thickness, rubs, then the chip grows thin to thick. The cutter lifts the work, so a lightly held job can chatter. Down milling (climb milling) has the feed with the cutter. The tooth starts at high chip thickness and the chip falls thick to thin. Cutting force presses the work onto the table, giving a better finish and longer tool life. The cutter also pulls the table, so backlash in the feed screw must be removed.

A dividing head indexes the work between cuts for flats, splines and gear teeth. For a simple dividing head with a 40:1 worm, one turn of the crank turns the work 1/40 rev. To divide a circle into N equal parts, the crank turns are 40/N. Example: N = 8 gives 40/8 = 5 crank turns per part. Use the index plate for fractional turns.

Choose drilling for a round hole along an axis. Choose reaming or boring only when the hole needs tight size or position. Choose milling for flat faces, slots and shaped contours. Face milling is common for a top surface; slab milling for a long flat; end milling for a pocket. A drill press feeds the drill by hand or power along a fixed axis; a milling machine feeds the table under a cutter. The feed screw and the cutter must be stiff because a long overhang bends. CNC milling is covered in Unit 6; the same cutter and feed logic applies there.

examples.question: A 20 mm diameter twist drill is to make a through hole in a 40 mm thick plate. Cutting speed is 25 m/min and feed is 0.15 mm/rev. The approach allowance is 5 mm. Find the spindle speed, feed rate, drilling time and material removal rate.
steps: Total travel = L + A = 40 + 5 = 45 mm. Drilling time = 45 / 59.7 = 0.754 min (about 45.2 s).
examples.answer: Spindle speed 397.9 rev/min (about 398 rev/min), feed rate 59.7 mm/min, drilling time 0.754 min, and MRR 18 750 mm³/min.
examples.check:
import math
D = 20.0
L = 40.0
v = 25.0
f = 0.15
A = 5.0
N = 1000 * v / (math.pi * D)
fr = f * N
t = (L + A) / fr
mrr = (math.pi / 4) * D * D * fr
print(f"{N:.1f}")
print(f"{fr:.1f}")
print(f"{t:.3f}")
print(f"{mrr:.0f}")

traps: Down milling needs backlash removed; otherwise the cutter pulls the table and the job jumps.
Spindle speed uses drill diameter D, not plate thickness L. Thickness enters only the time.
Counterboring is cylindrical for a socket-head screw; countersinking is conical for a flat-head screw.
In up milling the chip starts thin and ends thick; in down milling it starts thick and ends thin.
Simple indexing crank turns = 40/N, not N/40.

quiz.q: What is the standard point angle of a general-purpose twist drill?
Why does a drill need an approach allowance before the full diameter cuts?
quiz.a: The 118° point and chisel edge touch first; the drill must travel before the full diameter reaches the workpiece.

quiz.q: A 12 mm drill runs at 30 m/min with feed 0.10 mm/rev. Find N and feed rate.
A dividing head has a 40:1 ratio. How many crank turns for 16 equal divisions?
Why does down milling usually give a better finish than up milling?
quiz.a: The chip starts thick, the tooth does not rub, and the cutting force presses the work onto the table; this reduces chatter and burnishing.

quiz.q: A slot must be cut in a shaft and the feed screw has visible backlash. Which milling direction is unsafe and why?
quiz.a: Down milling is unsafe because the cutter pulls the table in the feed direction; backlash lets the table jump and the cutter may break. Use up milling or remove backlash.

beyond: Not for the exam. High-speed drilling uses internal coolant channels and carbide drills with flatter points for cast iron and stacked sheets. Five-axis milling lets a short, stiff cutter reach a sculpted surface without long overhang. In production, tool-life data and adaptive feed control set the table feed from spindle load.
